title: Implement managed Nix build and closure-bound activation
goal: Implement the fail-closed managed Nix/NixOS build and activation path required by the canonical executor profile: repository/revision/control-release bound builds, exact system-closure receipts, separate build and activation effect classes, and receipt-bound activation that consumes only the already approved closure without reevaluating mutable source.

approval.note: This task implements and validates the managed build/activation contract. Any activation proof must use a disposable/non-production target; productive Heim-PC activation or switch requires a later separately revised and authorized task.

acceptance.assertion: Build and Activation are distinct effect classes: building may realize an immutable closure but cannot change the active system, while activation requires its own explicit authority and receipt.
Automated Nix/NixOS builds run only through a managed path that binds repository, exact source revision, Control Release Set, Nix inputs, resource budgets, leases, effect class and bounded receipts.
A successful build receipt exposes and binds the exact immutable NixOS system closure, exact source revision and Control Release Set digest used to produce it.

Activation consumes a reviewed build/activation receipt bound to the exact source revision, system closure, target and Activation effect class; a caller-supplied closure string or branch name alone is insufficient authority.
Next-boot and persistent activation interfaces accept only the prebuilt approved closure and cannot silently reevaluate Git, branches, locks or remote inputs between review and activation.
Missing, stale, mismatched or unauthorized activation authority is rejected before any host mutation; tests prove the denied path produces no activation effect.

After an authorized activation on a disposable/non-production target, independent live readback proves the running/booted system closure equals the exact approved closure; this evidence does not authorize a productive Heim-PC switch.
Entrypoints and scripts remain adapters to the canonical managed-build/activation contract and cannot maintain a hidden second source of desired state, closure selection or activation authority.

Normal, boot-critical and destructive effects are classified by possible effect rather than filename or stated intent; ambiguous cases escalate fail-closed and destructive storage/firmware effects cannot use the normal rebuild path.
Every activation receipt identifies the prior/rollback closure and an explicit recovery path; rollback semantics are tested without relying on mutable source reevaluation.

If a required activation or privilege primitive belongs to another canonical authority, the implementation uses that typed authority or creates an explicit dependency instead of duplicating a second truth or broad sudo/root shell path.

This task ends without productive nixos-rebuild switch, productive boot activation, reboot into a new production system, storage/EFI/Secure-Boot/firmware mutation, or any equivalent Heim-PC cutover effect unless the TaskSpec is later separately revised, reviewed and authorized.
Focused build/activation/effect-classification tests plus required repository CI are green on the exact reviewed head before merge.
